title: A New Framework for Interfacial Statistics: Exact n-Point Correlations of Gaussian Level Sets
authors: Aleksei M. Cherkasov, Kirill M. Gerke, Aleksey Khlyupin
abstract: We derive exact analytical expressions for higher-order correlations of Gaussian level-set interfaces, establishing a direct link between bulk field statistics and interface geometry. This framework enables efficient reconstruction of disordered media, detailed modeling of {Gaussian foams}---structured, double-thresholded interfaces with tunable morphology---and analysis of {memory-enhanced anisotropy} reflecting directional persistence in surface structure. These results open new possibilities for characterizing complex transport, guiding stochastic reconstructions, designing materials with desired properties, quantifying the information content of correlation functions and modelling directional processes on irregular boundaries.
summary: This paper introduces an exact mathematical framework to calculate higher-order correlation functions for interfaces derived from Gaussian random fields. By linking bulk field statistics to the geometry of the interfaces, the authors enable the reconstruction of complex, disordered media like Gaussian foams. This work provides powerful tools for characterizing directional memory and connectivity in random physical systems.
main_problem: Developing an exact analytical framework to calculate higher-order (n-point) correlation functions for interfaces defined by Gaussian level sets.
main_result: The framework establishes explicit, exact analytical links between bulk field statistics, binary field correlations, and the geometry of the interfaces, allowing for the reconstruction of disordered media.
method: Derivation of $n$-point correlation functions ($F_{n,i}$) using spectral representations and establishing recursive relationships between different correlation types ($G_2, S_2, F_{2,i}$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on Gaussian Random Fields (GRFs) $Y(\mathbf{r})$ and their resulting interfaces, which can model complex structures like Gaussian foams or porous media.
key_observables: Interface correlation functions ($F_{n,i}$), bulk field autocorrelation ($G_2$), and binary field autocorrelation ($S_2$).
important_parameters: The level set threshold ($\alpha$) and the regularization parameter ($\epsilon$) are key parameters defining the interface.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the underlying field is Gaussian, allowing for the derivation of exact analytical forms for the correlation functions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the relationship between the continuous field, the thresholded binary field, and the derived correlation functions, comparing analytical predictions with numerical reconstructions for various field types.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the interface via level sets, deriving the two-point correlation function ($F_{2,i}$) and linking it to bulk statistics, and then extending this methodology to higher-order ($F_{3,i}$ and beyond) correlations to study directional memory effects.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical framework for calculating higher-order correlations and reconstructing underlying fields from boundary data is highly relevant to understanding entanglement structure or boundary conditions in quantum many-body systems.
